newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney has "excellent" 1998 outlook - chairman.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney has "excellent" 1998 outlook - chairman.

text.p: Euro Disney has started 1997 well and has an "excellent" outlook for 1998 which will help it meeting its royalty payments to Walt Disney Co from 1999, its chairman said on Sunday.

Gilles Pelisson, who became chairman earlier this year after Philippe Bourguignon jumped ship to head the Club Mediterannee holiday resort organisation, told le Journal du Dimanche that the company was reviewing ticket prices even though the absence of inflation made price rises difficult.
He said that a direct rail link between the Disneyland Paris site in Marne-La-Vallee and London would bring in an additional 800 British visitors per day.

Euro Disney, which celebrated its fifth anniversary on Saturday with a big show and parade featuring Barbara Hendricks, Roy Disney and 1,500 children from all over Europe, has to pay some 15 billion francs to Walt Disney Co from 1999.
"We are well aware of the importance of our debt and we are studying the best solutions. But we do not have a knife at our throat," Pelisson said.
"The year 1997 has started well and the outlook for 1998 is excellent, with the World Cup soccer championships in France which will be profitable to all tourism and leisure activities," he added.
